q: In a Dagster 1.13 project, my component's defs.yaml uses `description: "token={{ env.API_TOKEN }}"` and API_TOKEN is not set anywhere. What do `dg check yaml --validate-requirements` and `dg check defs` do, and what ends up in the asset description?
a: Both pass. An unset `{{ env.X }}` does not fail at load; it silently renders as None (whole-value template) or the string 'None' inside an interpolated string, so the description becomes 'token=None'. --validate-requirements only checks that the variable is declared under requirements.env, not that it is set. Verified on dagster 1.13.28.
trap: It fails validation/load with a missing environment variable error (the skill itself says env vars 'must exist at load time').

q: A defs/ module contains a module-level `@dg.asset` and also a `@dg.definitions` function returning `dg.Definitions(...)`. After `dg list defs`, which assets show up and is there a warning?
a: Only the assets in the Definitions returned by the @dg.definitions function load; the module-scope @dg.asset is skipped with no warning (reproduced). Keep @dg.definitions functions in their own module.
trap: Both load and merge, or Dagster warns/raises about the duplicate or skipped definition.

q: A defs.yaml has `post_processing: assets: [{attributes: {kinds: [b], tags: {y: '2'}}}]` and the component already sets `kinds: [a]` and `tags: {x: '1'}` on its asset. What are the final kinds and tags, and does `dg check yaml` validate the post_processing keys?
a: Default `operation: merge` merges only tags and metadata, so tags become {x, y} but kinds is replaced: {b} only (same for deps, owners, group_name). `operation: replace` replaces everything. `dg check yaml` does not validate post_processing contents (its schema is just `object`); bad keys such as key_prefix fail only in `dg check defs`.
trap: kinds {a, b} (merged) and `dg check yaml` catches bad post_processing attributes.

q: I wrote a custom StateBackedComponent as `@dataclass class X(dg.StateBackedComponent)` with `defs_state: ResolvedDefsStateConfig = DefsStateConfigArgs.local_filesystem()` (copied from the Dagster docstring) and every dg command now errors. What is wrong and what is the fix?
a: Dataclasses on Python 3.11+ reject the unhashable pydantic default: `ValueError: mutable default ... DefsStateConfigArgs ... use default_factory`. Use `field(default_factory=DefsStateConfigArgs.local_filesystem)`. Also add `dg.Resolvable` to the bases, because StateBackedComponent is not Resolvable and otherwise defs.yaml attributes are rejected ('Additional properties are not allowed').
trap: Suggests a missing entry point/reinstall, or a wrong management_type enum, or that the snippet is fine as written.

q: I added a `[project.entry-points] "dagster_dg_cli.registry_modules"` entry to pyproject.toml of my uv-managed Dagster project. Do I need `uv pip install -e .`, and what happens to the `registry_modules` list in [tool.dg.project]?
a: With current uv, plain `uv sync` detects the pyproject change and reinstalls the package, registering the entry point (verified, uv 0.13.6). Once an entry point exists, dg ignores `[tool.dg.project] registry_modules` entirely, and discovers only objects exposed in the entry-point module's own namespace (so classes must be re-exported in components/__init__.py, which `dg scaffold component` then does). Scaffolded projects don't need an entry point at all.
trap: 'uv sync will not reinstall the package; you must run uv pip install -e .' and that both mechanisms are combined.

q: My `dg check defs` in CI behaves differently from production because code branches on `os.getenv('DAGSTER_IS_DEV_CLI')`. Why, and which dg commands set that variable?
a: The top-level `dg` group sets DAGSTER_IS_DEV_CLI=1 for every dg command (check defs, list defs, launch, check yaml...), not just `dg dev` (also set by `dagster dev`). `dg check defs` additionally sets DAGSTER_IS_DEFS_VALIDATION_CLI=1.
trap: Only `dg dev` sets DAGSTER_IS_DEV_CLI, so `dg check defs` sees the production code path.

q: I call `defs.map_asset_specs(lambda spec: spec.replace_attributes(partitions_def=pdef))` inside a Component.build_defs override. What happens in 1.13.28?
a: TypeError: `Definitions.map_asset_specs()` takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given; the signature is keyword-only (`func=`, optional `selection=`). It is also a preview API (PreviewWarning).
trap: It works and returns a Definitions with the mapped specs.

q: I want to run an asset with default backfill settings over a range of daily partitions locally using the dg CLI: `dg launch --assets my_asset --partition-range 2024-05-01...2024-05-07`. Will that work on Dagster 1.13.x, and what has to be true of the asset if not?
a: It fails with a CheckError. `dg launch` runs in-process (no daemon, no backfill) and --partition-range requires every selected asset to have BackfillPolicy.single_run(); multi_run or the default one-run-per-partition policy are rejected and need the UI or `dagster job backfill` with a daemon.
trap: That dg launch queues a backfill that creates one run per partition (handled by the daemon).

q: An asset uses backfill_policy=dg.BackfillPolicy.single_run() with a daily partitions_def. In the body I call context.partition_key and return a DataFrame. What goes wrong when it is backfilled over several days, and how do you fix it?
a: Two failures: context.partition_key raises DagsterInvariantViolationError for a run covering a range (use partition_time_window, partition_key_range or partition_keys), and returning a value fails at handle-output because the default filesystem I/O manager cannot persist one object for multiple partitions. Write the data yourself and return None or dg.MaterializeResult(metadata=...). A 3-day range logs 1 step and 3 materializations.
trap: Thinking Dagster fans the value out per partition or that partition_key returns the first key.

q: A daily-partitioned asset has a schedule built with build_schedule_from_partitioned_job(job, hour_of_day=1, minute_of_hour=30). On 2024-05-20 at 01:30 the tick fires. Which partition does it run, and what changes the answer?
a: 2024-05-19, the latest completed partition (default end_offset=0). Setting end_offset=1 on the DailyPartitionsDefinition makes the same tick run 2024-05-20. hour_of_day/minute_of_hour only shift tick time, not the chosen partition.
trap: Running the partition for the current date (2024-05-20), or adjusting hour_of_day to change which partition is selected.

q: A downstream daily asset takes `up: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]` from an hourly upstream using a UPathIOManager-based I/O manager (the default filesystem one). Only 3 of the 24 hourly partitions for the day exist. What happens, and how do you let the downstream run?
a: Loading raises (FileNotFoundError, wrapped in DagsterExecutionLoadInputError) because missing partitions are errors by default. Put allow_missing_partitions=True in the consuming input's metadata: ins={'up': dg.AssetIn(metadata={'allow_missing_partitions': True})}; the dict then contains just the 3 present keys.
trap: That the input silently contains whatever exists, or that the flag goes on the upstream asset or I/O manager config.

q: Inside an I/O manager's load_input, I want the table name stored in the upstream asset's metadata, and also a value that the upstream asset reported via MaterializeResult(metadata=...). What do context.definition_metadata, context.upstream_output.definition_metadata and context.upstream_output.output_metadata give me?
a: InputContext.definition_metadata is the metadata on the consuming AssetIn/In (not the upstream asset's). upstream_output.definition_metadata is the upstream asset's definition metadata (use it for table names). upstream_output.output_metadata is {} during load_input: runtime metadata from MaterializeResult/Output is event-log only and not visible to I/O managers.
trap: That context.definition_metadata in load_input holds the upstream asset's metadata, and that MaterializeResult metadata can be read back via upstream_output.output_metadata.

q: In Dagster 1.13 I have a daily partitioned job and a hand-written schedule. How do I compute 'the latest partition key as of this tick' for `RunRequest(partition_key=...)`, and what must I not pass?
a: Wrap the lookup in `with dg.partition_loading_context(effective_dt=context.scheduled_execution_time): key = partitions_def.get_last_partition_key()`. `get_last_partition_key()` takes no arguments in 1.13.28, and `current_time=` raises a TypeError.
trap: `partitions_def.get_last_partition_key(current_time=context.scheduled_execution_time)`, the older signature.

q: I have a `@dg.run_failure_sensor` in code location `alerts` that should also watch jobs in code location `analytics`. I set `monitored_jobs=[dg.CodeLocationSelector(location_name='analytics')]`. Will failures of jobs in `alerts` still trigger it?
a: No. Once `monitored_jobs` is set, same-location runs match only listed job definitions or selectors, so a list of only other locations' selectors stops watching the home location. Add `dg.CodeLocationSelector(location_name='alerts')` too. Setting both `monitored_jobs` and `monitor_all_code_locations=True` raises 'Cannot specify both'.
trap: The selectors add to the default own-location monitoring, so `alerts` is still covered.

q: I want a downstream asset to materialize only after all three of its upstream assets have updated each cycle. Which built-in AutomationCondition do I use, and which one is the common wrong choice?
a: Use `AutomationCondition.on_cron(cron)`; its cron tick acts as a synchronization barrier and it requires every upstream to update within the tick. `eager()` fires when any dependency updates. Do not hand-build 'all_deps_match(newly_updated().since(...))', which has no barrier and can desynchronize indefinitely. `on_cron` also defaults to UTC unless `cron_timezone` is passed.
trap: `eager()` (it triggers on any upstream), or a custom `all_deps_match(newly_updated())` condition.

q: I subclassed `dg.AutomationCondition` with a custom `evaluate()` and attached it to an asset. It never evaluates, or errors in the daemon. What do I have to add, and what are the limits?
a: Custom Python conditions only evaluate on a sensor with `use_user_code_server=True` (e.g. `AutomationConditionSensorDefinition(name, target=..., use_user_code_server=True)`), since the daemon can't import user code. That sensor is capped at 500 assets/checks, is beta, and cannot target asset jobs. `default_condition` is only valid with `use_user_code_server=True`.
trap: The default_automation_condition_sensor evaluates custom conditions automatically once toggled on, or a plain @dg.sensor can evaluate them.

q: Using Dagster 1.13 declarative automation with `eager()` on a daily-partitioned asset, 30 historical partitions are missing. How many partitions does eager request, and how do I make it cover older ones?
a: Only the latest time partition, because eager/on_cron/on_missing all start with `in_latest_time_window()`. To widen, `.without(AutomationCondition.in_latest_time_window())` or `.replace(in_latest_time_window(), in_latest_time_window(timedelta(days=N)))` (string-label replace also works). Static and dynamic partitions are not limited to the latest.
trap: It requests all missing partitions (a backfill), or the fix is a backfill policy.

q: Writing a pytest for a downstream asset `def down(up): ...` in Dagster 1.13: what is wrong with `dg.materialize_to_memory([down], resources={"io_manager": dg.FilesystemIOManager(...)})`, and what changes if `down` instead declares `deps=[up]`?
a: Two problems: passing an explicit IO manager to materialize_to_memory raises DagsterInvariantViolationError (it forces mem_io_manager); and with a parameter dependency the upstream asset definition must be in the list or you get DagsterInvalidDefinitionError 'Input asset ... is not produced by any of the provided asset ops'. With `deps=[up]` the upstream need not be listed.
trap: Believing materialize_to_memory accepts an io_manager override, or that listing only the asset under test is enough for parameter-based dependencies.

q: An `@dg.asset_check(asset=orders, blocking=True)` returns `AssetCheckResult(passed=False)`; another returns `passed=False, severity=WARN`. In a job that also materializes a downstream asset of `orders`, what runs and what does `dg.materialize(...)` do with default arguments?
a: ERROR-severity (default) failure: the check step fails with DagsterAssetCheckFailedError ('1 blocking asset check failed with ERROR severity'), downstream assets do not execute, and dg.materialize raises that error because raise_on_error=True by default (use raise_on_error=False to inspect). WARN severity never blocks: downstream runs and the run succeeds.
trap: Thinking any failed blocking check stops downstream regardless of severity, or that a check failure only flags the UI and downstream still runs.

q: I want to use the new Dagster 1.12+ FreshnessPolicy.time_window(fail_window=timedelta(hours=24)) on an asset in a local OSS project. What extra setup is needed, do I need a sensor or schedule, and what happened to the old FreshnessPolicy class?
a: Freshness policies are preview and off by default: add `freshness:\n  enabled: True` to dagster.yaml (instance config key defaults to disabled). No sensor or schedule is required, unlike build_last_update_freshness_checks. The pre-1.6 class was renamed LegacyFreshnessPolicy; the name FreshnessPolicy now refers to the new API (time_window with fail_window >= 60s and warn_window < fail_window, or cron).
trap: Using FreshnessPolicy(maximum_lag_minutes=...) legacy kwargs or build_last_update_freshness_checks plus a sensor, or assuming policies work without enabling the instance flag.

q: I need a resource that wraps a foreign client class (e.g. `GitHub(token)`) with a config field, and an asset that receives the built client. Which base class and annotation do I use in Dagster 1.13 given the docs mention `ConfigurableResourceFactory` and `dg.Resource[T]`?
a: Subclass `dg.ConfigurableResource[GitHub]` and implement `create_resource(self, context) -> GitHub`; annotate the asset parameter `dg.ResourceParam[GitHub]`. `dg.ConfigurableResourceFactory` and `dg.Resource` are not exported from dagster in 1.13.28 (hasattr returns False), even though some docs pages use those names.
trap: Writing `class X(dg.ConfigurableResourceFactory[T])` and `dg.Resource[T]` from the docs page, which raise AttributeError on import/use.

q: In run-config YAML for an asset whose Config has an `enum.Enum` field and a pydantic discriminated union (`pet: Cat | Dog = Field(discriminator='pet_type')`), how are the enum value and the union written, and what happens with unknown keys?
a: Enums are written by member name (`Bob: GUEST`, not the value `guest`; the value form raises DagsterInvalidConfigError). A discriminated union nests under the discriminator value (`pet: {cat: {meows: 10}}`; the flat `{pet_type: cat, meows: 10}` form fails). Unknown keys fail with DagsterInvalidConfigError unless the model subclasses dg.PermissiveConfig. Asset config lives under `ops: {<asset_name>: {config: ...}}` and dg.RunConfig's first positional argument is `ops`.
trap: Writing the enum's value and the flat pydantic-style union form, or expecting extra keys to be silently ignored.

q: I changed `[tool.dg.project]` settings and need `dg` to use a non-default virtualenv, e.g. `../.venvs/my-project`. Where must I set `DG_PROJECT_PYTHON_EXECUTABLE` for it to take effect, and does exporting it in my shell work?
a: It must be in the project-root `.env` file (relative paths resolve against the project root). dg reads it via dotenv_values on `<project_root>/.env` only (dagster_dg_core/context.py project_python_executable); exporting it in the shell has no effect. Default is `<project_root>/.venv`, and `--use-active-venv` is the alternative.
trap: Exporting the variable in the shell or setting it in pyproject.toml.

q: I have a fresh Dagster 1.13.28 OSS deployment whose dagster.yaml sets only `storage:` (no run_coordinator section). A sensor fires 25 runs at once. Which run coordinator is in effect and how do the runs behave?
a: QueuedRunCoordinator is the default. Runs go to QUEUED and the daemon's run-queue daemon dequeues them, with at most max_concurrent_runs (default 10) in progress at once. -1 removes the limit, 0 halts launching. Without a running daemon the runs strand in QUEUED. DefaultRunCoordinator applies only if configured explicitly.
trap: DefaultRunCoordinator launches all 25 immediately with no queue or limit, and queueing needs `run_coordinator: QueuedRunCoordinator` or `run_queue:` configured first.

q: A Pipes external script calls `context.report_asset_materialization(metadata={'schema': {'type': 'table_schema', 'raw_value': [{'name': 'id', 'type': 'int'}]}})` in 1.13.28. What happens, and what should raw_value be?
a: The orchestration side rejects the list (ParameterCheckError: 'table_schema_value' not a Mapping) in the message-handler thread. The traceback goes to stderr, the step still succeeds, and the metadata is silently dropped. raw_value must be `{'columns': [{'name':..., 'type':...}]}`. Likewise table_column_lineage needs `{'deps_by_column': {col: [{'asset_key':..., 'column_name':...}]}}`.
trap: A bare list of column dicts works (as the docs show), or the step fails loudly. Lineage keyed by `table_column_lineage` with `column`.
src: pipes-external-execution.md:138,147 (skill is wrong; verified by running a PipesSubprocessClient asset)

q: I want `concurrency.runs.max_concurrent_runs` and `run_retries.max_retries` in dagster.yaml to come from environment variables via `{env: NAME}`. Will that load?
a: No for those fields: concurrency.runs.*, concurrency.pools.default_limit, run_retries.*, run_monitoring.*, code_servers.*, sensors/schedules threading, telemetry, retention and python_logs are plain int/bool/str and fail instance load with 'Invalid scalar'. `{env:}` works only for source-typed fields (run_coordinator config values, storage connection fields, compute-log manager config, auto_materialize). Set literals or template the file at deploy time.
trap: Every dagster.yaml scalar accepts `{env: VAR}`.
src: operations-and-debugging.md:46 (skill is wrong; verified by loading instances)

q: I add `pool="db"` to an asset but configure no pool limit anywhere. Does it throttle? And if a run holding the only slot of a limit-1 pool is cancelled, what frees the slot?
a: No throttling: a pool with no configured limit is unlimited. A limit comes from `concurrency.pools.default_limit`, `dagster instance concurrency set db 1`, or the UI. Slots held by cancelled or failed runs are not released automatically; set `run_monitoring.enabled: true` plus `run_monitoring.free_slots_after_run_end_seconds` (unset by default, handled by the monitoring daemon), otherwise free them manually in Deployment > Concurrency.
trap: Pools default to a limit of 1, and slots are released when the run ends or is cancelled.

q: I'm wiring a custom (non-GitHub) CI to deploy to Dagster+ with the `dg` CLI, in stages: start the session, build and push the image, then tell Dagster+ to update the code locations. Which commands do I run, and what happens if the last stage is just `dg plus deploy`?
a: `dg plus deploy start`, then `dg plus deploy build-and-push`, then `dg plus deploy finish`. Bare `dg plus deploy` (no subcommand) runs the whole start, build and finish sequence end to end, and init deletes and recreates the statedir, so running it as the last stage redoes everything instead of finalizing. `start` uses `--target-path` (no `--project-dir`).
trap: Run `dg plus deploy` as the final step, as the docs and the skill's CI snippet say. Or use `--project-dir=.` on `start`.

q: On a fresh laptop I run `dg plus login` or `dg plus config set --organization acme --deployment prod`. Which file does the CLI write the config to, and what breaks if an old `~/.dagster_cloud_cli/config` also has Plus settings?
a: It writes a `[cli.plus]` table in the user dg config `~/.config/dg.toml` (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dg.toml`, or the `DG_CLI_CONFIG` path). It does not create `~/.dagster_cloud_cli/config`; that legacy file is only read or updated if it already exists. If Plus config exists in both files, the CLI raises "Found Dagster Plus config in both ... Please consolidate".
trap: It writes `~/.dagster_cloud_cli/config`, shared with the dagster-cloud CLI.

q: For Dagster+ branch deployments, I want at most 5 concurrent runs per PR and 100 across all PRs. Is this a deployment setting I set with `dg api deployment settings set`, and what role does it need?
a: No. Branch-deployment concurrency is organization-scoped: `max_concurrent_branch_deployment_runs` (default 50; max 500 Hybrid / 50 Serverless), `max_concurrent_runs_per_branch_deployment` (default null, must be <= the global cap) and `branch_deployment_tag_concurrency_limits`. Edit them in Organization Settings > Advanced or with `dg api organization settings get/set`, as Organization Admin. Both run limits apply at once. Full-deployment settings do not govern branch deployments.
trap: Put `concurrency.runs.max_concurrent_runs` in the deployment settings YAML for the branch deployment. Or answer that the per-branch limit overrides the global one.

q: In Dagster 1.13, I port old code: `@asset(freshness_policy=LegacyFreshnessPolicy(maximum_lag_minutes=5))`, `AssetOut(legacy_freshness_policy=...)` and `@observable_source_asset(auto_observe_interval_minutes=10)`. What does each do?
a: The first raises ParameterCheckError, because `freshness_policy=` on `@asset` and `AssetSpec` accepts only the new `dg.FreshnessPolicy`; legacy policies go through the deprecated `legacy_freshness_policy=`, which still works on `@asset` and `AssetSpec`. The other two are removed in 1.13 but are silently swallowed by `**kwargs`: no error, no effect. Use `automation_condition=` plus schedules/sensors or freshness checks.
trap: Assumes all three still work with warnings, or that removed args raise TypeError.

q: I'm on Dagster 1.13 and need to model external (not Dagster-produced) assets. Which constructs from older tutorials will fail, and what's the replacement?
a: `external_assets_from_specs` and `external_asset_from_spec` are no longer exported and fail on import. A bare `deps=dg.AssetKey('x')` fails (AssetKey is no longer iterable; wrap it in a list or use `dg.AssetDep`). Pass `dg.AssetSpec(...)` objects straight into `Definitions(assets=[...])`.
trap: `external_assets_from_specs([...])` (still deprecated-but-working in 1.12) or `SourceAsset`.

q: I converted a legacy Dagster project to the `dg` layout by adding a `dagster_dg_cli.registry_modules` entry point to its pyproject.toml, then ran `uv sync`, but `dg list registry-modules` doesn't show my components module. Why, and how do I fix it?
a: With current uv (0.13.x), plain `uv sync` detects the pyproject.toml change and reinstalls the project, registering the entry point; `uv pip install -e .` or `uv sync --reinstall-package <pkg>` also work but are not required. (Once an entry point exists, [tool.dg.project] registry_modules is ignored.)
trap: `uv sync` will not reinstall; you must run `uv pip install -e .`

q: Using dagster-sling with the default `DagsterSlingTranslator` (target_prefix "target") and a replication stream `public.accounts`, what asset key does the generated asset get and what is its upstream dep key? How would you reference that asset from a downstream `@dg.asset`?
a: The key is a multi-segment path ['target','public','accounts'] (displayed `target/public/accounts`). The dep is ['public','accounts']. Reference it with `deps=[dg.AssetKey(['target','public','accounts'])]` or by overriding via `meta.dagster.asset_key` in replication.yaml. Derived from `_default_asset_key_fn` and `clean_name_lower_with_dots`. (If the stream sets `object:`, the key uses the object path.)
trap: A single flat key `target_public_accounts` depending on `public_accounts`, which is the wrong claim in the translator docstring and the skill.

q: In a `DbtProjectComponent` defs.yaml, how do you make dbt source tests load as Dagster asset checks, since the Python `DagsterDbtTranslatorSettings` object is not available in YAML? Does the component enable code references by default?
a: Set `attributes.translation_settings: {enable_source_tests_as_checks: true}`. The component's settings class `DagsterDbtComponentTranslatorSettings` defaults `enable_code_references` to True, unlike the Python `DagsterDbtTranslatorSettings` (False). Verified in dagster-dbt 0.29.28 source.
trap: It cannot be set from YAML (use `@dbt_assets` with `DagsterDbtTranslatorSettings`), or a made-up key such as `enable_source_tests_as_checks` under `translation`.

q: You want Power BI semantic models to be refreshable and materializable from Dagster, and you are using dagster-powerbi's Component in defs.yaml. How do you enable that without writing Python wrappers?
a: Set `enable_semantic_model_refresh` on `PowerBIWorkspaceComponent`: `true` for all semantic models, or a list of model names. Equivalent switches: `TableauComponent.enable_embedded_datasource_refresh` / `enable_published_datasource_refresh`, `LookerComponent.pdt_builds`. Verified in the 0.29.28 wheel source.
trap: BI assets from `load_powerbi_asset_specs` or the Component are always observable-only; you must call `build_semantic_model_refresh_asset_definition` in Python.

q: What does `DbtCliResource` use as its dbt executable by default in dagster-dbt 0.29.28 (Dagster 1.13.28), and what happens to `.fetch_row_counts()` when that executable is the Fusion engine?
a: `dbtf` if it is found on PATH (dbt Fusion), otherwise `dbt`. When the invocation is Fusion, `fetch_row_counts()` logs a warning and returns the events unchanged, so no row_count metadata is attached. Verified in dagster_dbt/core/resource.py and core/dbt_event_iterator.py.
trap: The default is always the string 'dbt', and row counts are fetched on any engine.

q: With dagster-fivetran, what is the default effect of Dagster triggering a connector sync on the connector's Fivetran schedule, and which two `FivetranWorkspace` settings change the default behaviors around that sync?
a: By default (`disable_schedule_on_trigger=True`) the first Dagster-triggered sync sets the connector's schedule to manual, turning off Fivetran's own scheduling. Setting `disable_schedule_on_trigger=False` keeps both. `retry_on_reschedule` (default True) controls whether a quota-based reschedule raises RetryRequested (False keeps polling in the same step). Both default values confirmed in resources.py.
trap: Dagster just calls the sync API and leaves the Fivetran schedule untouched. Or: the polling sensor is required to avoid duplicate runs.
